source: Lilly Christian Astrology 1647 first edition, Wellcome b30338724
title: Of the Fortune and condition of Brethren
scope: Historical and gender-stereotyped alleged outcomes for siblings, no real-life survival, wealth or relationship validations.

groups.source_group: Original CXIX chapter heading and selection of sibling significators

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXIX Of the Fortune and condition of Brethren
claims.meaning_historical_only: A new independent numbered chapter follows the sibling-number sign table on PDF600/printed566, concerning siblings' conditions.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: From the affection of the Significators
claims.meaning_historical_only: Lilly derives these alleged sibling life outcomes from their astrological signifiers' favorable or unfavorable state.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if all or the greater part be strong
claims.meaning_historical_only: The author permits the majority rather than requiring every sibling indicator to be strong.
The source associates the strong-indicator configuration with siblings' happiness/fortune, without independent human testimony.
It separately asserts sibling longevity; no actual survival data or prospective validation are supplied.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: honour and Wealth to the Brothers and Sisters
claims.meaning_historical_only: The source also alleges reputation and resources for siblings, distinct from sibling count and lifespan.
Lilly adds an alleged benefit to the chart's native from fortunate siblings, not merely good for those siblings.

groups.source_group: Unfavorable planetary conditions and mixed strength

claims.meaning_historical_only: The text treats weak sibling indicators as a broad contrary-case source instead of only no positive evidence.
It assigns adverse sibling circumstances in the weak case without quantifying which particular outcome is absent or bad.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: If part be weak and part strong
claims.meaning_historical_only: A partly favorable/partly unfavorable set of sibling significators is explicitly considered.
The mixed case is alleged to produce moderate fortunes for some siblings rather than a universal bad verdict.
Other siblings in the same mixed chart may allegedly experience hardships, allowing differing sibling outcomes.

groups.source_group: Moon strong and Mars weak: historically sister-favorable disparity

claims.meaning_historical_only: The sibling comparative rule is further framed by a mostly strong significator context, not just one lone lunar placement.
A strongly placed Moon is one required condition of the author's sister-favorable comparison.
The counterpart requires Mars weak, so the source is explicitly relational rather than Moon-only.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sisters more happy then the Brothers
claims.meaning_historical_only: Lilly claims comparatively better outcomes for sisters; it is a period gender category claim with no human validation.

groups.source_group: Mars strong and Moon weak: historically brother-favorable disparity

claims.meaning_historical_only: The author reverses the earlier comparison when Mars is strong.
A weak and afflicted Moon is the corresponding required opposite condition.
The source attributes better advancement/preferment to brothers under this combination, without any observed cohort.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: to live better then the Sisters
claims.meaning_historical_only: It separately alleges brothers' generally better material circumstances compared to sisters, not an actual measured difference.

groups.source_group: Following printed CXX unity/concord: navigation only

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXX Of the unity or concord ... Brethren and Sisters
claims.meaning_historical_only: Printed CXX begins at the top of following original PDF601/printed567 and is separate from CXIX sibling fortune.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: benevolent aspect ... Lord of the first and third
claims.meaning_historical_only: The beginning of the following harmony method is noted only to verify the chapter seam, not admitted as a CXIX rule.
